message_source_quote: Raman et al.'s white-bear steering extracted its direction from WorkspaceBench's own `directed_modulation` bank. My direction is built from scratch from self-authored pairs with no link to the benchmark.
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed a think/don't-think "white-bear" stance vector lifts implied concepts in the J-lens, but their vector came from WorkspaceBench's `directed_modulation` bank. My contribution is that the stance is a **model-level, prompt-invariant direction**
rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. (2026)'s white-bear steering as the prior method, note that it derived its direction from WorkspaceBench's directed_modulation bank, and claim the same novelty: a self-authored, prompt-invariant stance direction with no link to the benchmark that reproduces and slightly exceeds the bank direction's gain (cosine 0.89-0.91, matching norms). The message adds a specific numeric comparison (0.78 vs 0.56 at k=7) not spelled out in the write-up, but this is a number/mechanism detail excluded from material differences by the codebook, so the source, overlap, and novelty framing are equivalent across both documents.
